import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Energy-critical NLS in three dimensions.

This file states an a priori estimate for the energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation on $ℝ^3$.
By 'soft' arguments, this bound implies global well-posedness in the energy space, scattering,
asymptotic completeness, and uniform regularity (all of which are less elementary to state).
This is remarked on p. 770 and p. 793 in the referenced article which first proved the a priori bound.

The main theorem is:
- `NLS_apriori`: a bound on the space-time $L^10$ norm in terms of the initial energy for local
  smooth solutions to the NLS equation.

## References
* [Colliander, Keel, Staffilani, Takaoka, Tao](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2008.167.767),
  Annals of Mathematics 167 (2008) proves the a priori estimate, and thereby, global well-posedness.
-/

open Set ContDiff EuclideanGeometry Laplacian MeasureTheory

namespace NLSCritical

/--
A smooth solution to the NLS equation on the time interval $[-l, l]$.
We additionally require that $x ↦ u(t,x)$ is Schwartz for all $t$ in the interval.
-/
structure LocalSchwartzSolution (l : ℝ) where
  u : ℝ → ℝ^3 → ℂ
  smooth : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (Function.uncurry u) (Icc (-l) l ×ˢ univ)
  schwartz : ∀ t ∈ Icc (-l) l, ∃ f : (SchwartzMap (ℝ^3) ℂ), u t = f
  L10_loc : IntegrableOn (fun t ↦ (∫ x, ‖u t x‖^10)) (Icc (-l) l)
  C0H1 : ∃ v : C(ℝ, ℝ^3 →₂[volume] ℝ^3 →L[ℝ] ℂ), ∀ t ∈ Icc (-l) l, ∀ᵐ x, fderiv ℝ (u t ·) x = v t x
  solution : ∀ t ∈ Icc (-l) l, ∀ x, Complex.I * (deriv (u · x) t) + Δ (u t) x = ‖u t x‖^4 * (u t x)

/--
The Hamiltonian of the energy-critical NLS in $ℝ^3$.
-/
noncomputable def energy (u : ℝ^3 → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x, (1 / 2) * ‖fderiv ℝ u x‖^2 + (1 / 6) * ‖u x‖^6

/--
The space-time $L^10$ norm, restricted to the time interval $[-l,l]$.
-/
noncomputable def L10_local (l : ℝ) (u : ℝ → ℝ^3 → ℂ) :=
  ∫ t in Icc (-l) l, (∫ x, ‖u t x‖^10)

/--
The $L^10_{t,x}$ a priori estimate for local schwartz solutions.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 35]
theorem NLS_apriori :
    ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, ∀ l > 0, ∀ s : LocalSchwartzSolution l,
    L10_local l s.u ≤ f (energy (s.u 0)) := by
  sorry

end NLSCritical

reformulations.difference: The declaration states an a priori estimate for local Schwartz solutions on symmetric compact time intervals, rather than directly stating global well-posedness and scattering for arbitrary energy-class data.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Section 4.1 explicitly reduces the paper's global theorem to uniform spacetime bounds for Schwartz solutions on compact intervals. Local well-posedness, uniqueness, continuation, and approximation using the perturbation theorem supply the reverse implication; the global result immediately bounds its local restrictions. Time translation centres an arbitrary nondegenerate compact interval at zero. L10_local is the tenth power of the norm, matching the integral in the paper's spacetime estimate, so the absent tenth root does not change the assertion.

reformulations.difference: The helper uses the operator norm of the real-linear differential ℝ³ →L[ℝ] ℂ, not the Hilbert–Schmidt norm whose square is the sum of the three squared complex partial derivatives. Thus it is an equivalent energy-control functional, not literally the Hamiltonian described in the docstring.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing Eop for this helper and H for the paper's Hamiltonian, Eop(u) ≤ H(u) ≤ 3 Eop(u) for Schwartz u; these inequalities were proved in the scratch experiments. Their use in the sole theorem is equivalent, even though its bounding function is not required to be monotone. For a nonzero Schwartz solution, Galilean boosts u_v(t,x) = exp(i(v·x−|v|²t))u(t,x−2tv) preserve the spacetime integral. Both initial energy functionals vary continuously under these boosts and tend to infinity along an unbounded boost parameter, so each can be raised to any prescribed level at least its original value. Consequently an Eop-bound f gives an H-bound f by raising Eop to H, and an H-bound g gives an Eop-bound e ↦ g(3e) by raising H to 3Eop. Zero solutions are handled by taking nonnegative bounds. This establishes equivalence of the a priori estimates, not equality of the functionals.

sources_consulted: Colliander, Keel, Staffilani, Takaoka and Tao, Annals of Mathematics 167 (2008), 767–865; https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2008.167.767 and the official article page https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2008/167-3/p03.

https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0402129 — v7 LaTeX source: Theorem 1.1, the Hamiltonian and spacetime-bound equations, §3.4 on local well-posedness and persistence of regularity, §4.1 on the Schwartz-solution reduction and energy-level suprema, and the concluding remarks.

review.notes: Checked all four declarations and all fields of LocalSchwartzSolution. The research solved tag agrees with the cited paper. Lean experiments in /workspace/review/boundaries.lean establish nonemptiness via zero solutions and integrability of the relevant spatial and energy integrands, ruling out unintended Bochner-integral defaults. The global continuous representative in C0H1 only encodes local homogeneous-H¹ continuity: its values outside the interval can be extended constantly from the endpoints. /workspace/review/norm_test.lean verifies an explicit differential with operator-norm square 1 and squared-gradient sum 2; energy_comparison.lean proves Eop ≤ H ≤ 3Eop. equivalence.lean proves the abstract bound-transfer equivalence under energy-level-raising hypotheses. The NLS-specific Galilean argument and full local/global equivalence were checked mathematically, not formalized in Lean.
